questions.question: What is the difference between a cell and a battery? Where is the energy stored?
questions.expected_answer: A cell is a single unit that stores energy in chemicals inside it. A battery is two or more cells joined together, positive to negative, like the two cells in a torch or the six cells in a car battery.

questions.question: Describe how to connect a cell, wires and a bulb so that the bulb lights. What does a switch do?
questions.expected_answer: Join one wire from the positive terminal of the cell to one side of the bulb holder, and a second wire from the other side of the bulb holder back to the negative terminal, making a complete loop. A switch opens and closes a gap in the circuit: closed, the bulb lights; open, it goes out.

questions.question: Explain how energy is transferred and changed in a torch.
questions.expected_answer: Energy is stored as chemical energy in the cells. When the switch is closed, it is transferred as electrical energy around the circuit to the bulb, which changes it into light energy and some heat energy.
